_comment: Hand-curated layer of docs/capabilities.json (capability-config.md §2 p.3). The emitter (stapel_workspaces/_capabilities.py) merges this over the derived axes; this module's settings namespace (STAPEL_WORKSPACES) mostly carries merge-registries and tuning. One CTO-facing axis as of the mandate-model vardict (2026-08-03, org-program #85) — STREET_LANDING_MODE — curated below; provides/requires/extension_points still feed the capability catalog. Keep language business-facing — it surfaces in CTO conversations, not in code.
provides: Team workspaces and tenancy: personal and work workspaces with a role/capability mandate model (builtin owner/admin/member/viewer plus product roles declared in settings, namespaced capability strings with wildcard grants), email invitations with single-use tokens (public preview / decline / claim flow: an unregistered invitee gets a verified account via auth's login-grant seam), last-owner protection, per-workspace settings and storage quotas, member lifecycle events for business services (kick, role change), a billing entitlement seam that fails closed (an unreachable billing answers 503, not an unlimited plan, unless the deployment declares ALLOW_UNBILLED), plus internal service-to-service membership and capability checks — the foundational scope other modules attach their workspace_id to.

requires.reason: comm bus (workspace.* emits, workspaces.check_membership Function, user.registered consumer), JWT authentication, GDPR provider registry

emits the user.registered event that triggers personal-workspace creation and issues the authenticated sessions the workspace endpoints require; answers auth.issue_login_grant for the invitation claim step and auth.provision_user / auth.mfa_status for org provisioning and the require_mfa sweep; answers auth.admin_reset_password (>= 0.18) for the administrative password reset — which is where the credential work, the session revocation, the audit row and the refusal to touch a staff account live, because the caller knows who administers a workspace and nothing about who administers the deployment; answers auth.apply_first_login_policies (>= 0.17) when an organization has CONFIGURED first-login policies — that seam alone is fail-closed: an acceptance that cannot raise a demanded policy is refused (503) rather than admitting an unhardened member, while an organization that configured nothing never calls it at all; every other auth seam either degrades to an honest 503 (claim) or is never reached; decoupled via the comm bus

delivers the letters this module requests via request_notification: workspace.invitation (create, address with an account), workspace.invitation.new_user (create, address with none — >= 0.6.1, selected from 0.23), workspace.invitation.reminder (admin resend, >= 0.6.1), workspace.member_password_reset (>= 0.6.1) and the workspace.provisioned_account / workspace.mfa_* family; every one is best-effort — the workspace operation succeeds regardless, and an older notifications catalog drops the unknown type with a logged error

answers billing.check_entitlement for org creation and member-seat ceilings; the seam fails closed since 0.25 — a billing that is not installed, not routed or simply down answers 503 error.503.billing_unavailable rather than granting an unlimited plan, because those three look identical from here; a deployment that genuinely sells nothing says so once with STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ALLOW_UNBILLED"] and manage.py check (E011) refuses to boot silently either way; decoupled via the comm bus

the canonical source of a member's display name — this module stores only a name HINT typed at invite/provision time (WorkspaceMember.display_name_hint), never a second copy of the real field. Reads: MemberResponse.display_name resolves through the profiles seam (in-process Profile lookup first, then that module's public POST /batch over PROFILES_SERVICE_URL), falling back to the hint when profiles is absent, unreachable, or has no name yet. Writes (0.19): the roster's PATCH members/{id}/name sets Profile.display_name and publishes profile.changed, and both name-edit endpoints hold the value to that module's validate_display_name canon rather than a second rule of their own — profiles registers no comm Function and publishes no write-somebody-else's-name operation, so the write only exists in a process where profiles is mounted and answers error.503.profiles_unavailable where it is not. Never a hard import either way

extension_points.name: Workspace.settings
extension_points.summary: A JSON bag on every workspace, PATCHable through the workspace API — the sanctioned place for app-level per-workspace preferences without schema changes.

extension_points.name: AUTH_USER_MODEL
extension_points.summary: Standard Django user swap — owner/member/inviter FKs target settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL; the module resolves users via get_user_model(), never a concrete class.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every public view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamsMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

extension_points.name: role_capabilities
extension_points.summary: Declare product roles and their capability strings in STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ROLES"] (last-wins over the builtin four; owner is system-protected). Check them via has_capability/require_capability (in-service) or the workspaces.check_capability / check_membership comm Functions (cross-service, no import); frontends read GET /roles and my_capabilities.

extension_points.name: capability_levels
extension_points.summary: Raise individual capabilities to the high step-up level via STAPEL_WORKSPACES["CAPABILITY_LEVELS"] (merged over the builtin members.provision / workspace.security.manage); enforcement arrives with the provisioning wave.

STREET_LANDING_MODE.business_label: What an un-invited signup lands with
STREET_LANDING_MODE.summary: Controls what a freshly registered account gets when it showed up on its own (no invitation) — read by resolve_landing_workspace(user, origin="street"). "personal" (default) gives it its own Personal workspace and makes it that workspace's owner — the open self-serve / demo-cloud shape, unchanged from every release before this axis existed. "none" gives it no workspace at all: the account is a guest (permissions.is_guest) until an existing organization invites it — the closed-organization shape. Does not affect invited registrations, which always land through the separate accept-invitation path.
STREET_LANDING_MODE.behavior: personal: ensure_personal_workspace(user) runs, the account becomes OWNER of a new Personal workspace; none: no workspace is created, the account has zero memberships until invited.

role_at_least.intent: Role-ordering check — instead of hardcoding a role order.

get_membership.intent: Fetch a user's WorkspaceMember row (active by default; include_suspended=True also returns a suspended one, e.g. to render error.403.membership_suspended instead of a bare not-a-member 403) — defines what "active membership" means.

require_role.intent: Membership if the user holds at least a minimum role, else None — this module's own role-gate.

has_capability.intent: True if the user's active membership grants a capability — the everyday authorization check.

require_capability.intent: Membership if the user holds a capability, else None — capability-gate for a view.

has_active_mandate.intent: True if the user holds an active (accepted, non-suspended) membership ANYWHERE, workspace-agnostic — the primitive behind is_guest; use it when the question is "has this account joined anything at all", not "is it a member of workspace W".

has_active_mandate_for_id.intent: has_active_mandate addressed by user id rather than by user object — the form the workspaces.check_mandate comm provider needs, so the wire answer and the in-process one can never drift into two definitions of "active".

is_guest.intent: THE canonical guest predicate (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03): true for an authenticated user with no active mandate anywhere — an anonymous session qualifies by construction. Branch dashboards/onboarding on this, never on request.user.is_authenticated.

effective_roles.intent: Builtin roles merged with STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ROLES"] — read instead of merging the setting yourself.

effective_capability_levels.intent: Builtin capability step-up levels merged with the CAPABILITY_LEVELS override.

capability_level.intent: "standard"/"high" step-up level of a capability — check before gating on step-up.

capability_matches.intent: Match one granted capability string (wildcards "*" and "prefix.*") against a requested one — reach for this instead of writing your own prefix/wildcard comparison; stapel-core's cross-service consumer helper mirrors this exact semantics.

capabilities_for.intent: Granted capability strings of a role — primitive behind role_has_capability.

role_has_capability.intent: Does this role grant this capability, no membership needed — for role definitions/invite pickers.

role_rank.intent: Numeric rank of a role, or None — prefer role_at_least/role_exceeds_rank for yes/no.

role_exceeds_rank.intent: The invite/role-grant rank-guard (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03): true if a role outranks the acting role, so a product-defined role below admin that still carries members.invite/members.role.change/members.provision cannot hand out a rank above its own. Call this before creating any membership, invitation or provision row that assigns a role; unknown ranks fail closed.

create_workspace.intent: Create a workspace and atomically seed its owner membership — instead of a bare, ownerless row.

ensure_personal_workspace.intent: Idempotent get-or-create of a user's Personal workspace; prefer resolve_landing_workspace.

resolve_landing_workspace.intent: The canon landing-mandate policy (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03) for a freshly (re)appearing account — call this from a user.registered subscriber instead of unconditionally minting a personal workspace; reads STREET_LANDING_MODE and is a deliberate no-op for an invited origin, so a subscriber cannot double-mint or race the invite's own membership.

create_invitation.intent: Create a single-use, TTL'd invitation and deliver it best-effort — as workspace.invitation.new_user when the address has no account yet, workspace.invitation when it does.

invite_members.intent: Invite a batch of addresses — counts the plan's seats and writes the invitations in one locked transaction, so two batches cannot sell the same seat twice.

issue_invitation_login_grant.intent: Mint an auth-backed login grant for a not-yet-registered invitee's claim step (0.7).

revoke_invitation.intent: Withdraw a live invitation under the same compare-and-set lock as accept/decline, recording WHO withdrew it (revoked_by).

resend_invitation.intent: Re-deliver an invitation and extend its TTL — instead of editing fields by hand. Refuses with InvitationResendCooldown inside the per-address cooldown; keeps the invitee's existing token unless the deployment asked for rotation.

resend_cooldown_remaining.intent: Seconds before the invited address may be mailed about this invitation again (0 = now) — ask before offering a resend affordance, rather than discovering the 429.

decline_invitation.intent: The invitee's terminal "no" (≠ revoke), same row-lock as accept.

accept_invitation.intent: Resolve a pending invitation into a membership — entitlement check, first-login policies, emits together.

lock_workspace.intent: Take the workspace row lock every seat/owner write serializes on — call it before counting anything you are about to decide from.

change_member_role.intent: Write a member's new role with the last-owner invariant re-checked under the workspace lock — raises LastOwnerError instead of leaving an ownerless workspace.

remove_member.intent: Delete a membership under the same lock and invariant as change_member_role — returns (workspace, user, role) of what went.

apply_first_login_policies.intent: Demand an org's first-login steps of an account, failing closed.

security_settings_for.intent: Typed, defaulted view of Workspace.settings["security"] — instead of indexing the JSON bag directly.

provision_member.intent: Create an org-provisioned member end to end (debit, auth.provision_user, membership, credentials).

reconcile_provision_operations.intent: Retry the refunds a failed provisioning could not make — the queue manage.py reconcile_provisioning drains, so an orphan charge is a number somebody can act on.

reset_member_password.intent: Reset a member's password on the org's order, with the audit emit and security-signal letter.

suspend_member.intent: Suspend a membership without removing it (idempotent) — instead of writing suspended_at directly.

unsuspend_member.intent: Lift a membership suspension (idempotent) — counterpart of suspend_member.

enforce_require_mfa.intent: Sweep a workspace's members via auth.mfa_status, suspend the unenrolled, fail-open on an auth hiccup.

mfa_enforcement_for.intent: The workspace's MFA enforcement record (pending/enforcing/enforced/failed) — read it, not the settings flag, to answer whether MFA actually holds here.

verify_member_mfa.intent: Ask auth about one member's second factor and store the answer — returns None when auth could not be reached, which never counts as compliant.

record_member_mfa.intent: Persist one member's compliance answer (and suspend them for no_mfa when it is a no) — the per-member half the sweep and the events share.

retry_mfa_enforcement.intent: Idempotent re-sweep of every workspace not yet enforced — what manage.py enforce_workspace_mfa schedules.

mfa_admission_blocked.intent: Is this member barred by the workspace's require_mfa policy — the door the policy is enforced at, verifying on the spot when nobody has asked yet.

lift_no_mfa_suspensions.intent: Lift every no_mfa suspension in a workspace — call when require_mfa turns off.

suspend_memberships_without_mfa.intent: Per-user no_mfa suspension sweep wired to auth's user.mfa_disabled — call to force it on demand.

lift_no_mfa_suspensions_for_user.intent: Lift a user's no_mfa suspensions only, wired to auth's user.mfa_enabled.

suspend_memberships_for_deactivated_user.intent: Suspend every membership of a deactivated account, wired to auth's user.deactivated.

lift_deactivation_suspensions_for_user.intent: Reverse deactivation suspensions on reactivation, leaving no_mfa ones alone.

check_display_name.intent: Ask stapel-profiles' own name canon by name (profiles.validate_display_name) what a display name may contain; returns that module's error.400.display_name_* key or None. Anything here that accepts or writes a name goes through it, and this module keeps no second, differently-strict copy — that drift is what it exists to stop. Best-effort: no provider means no canon applied here, never a locally invented rule.

set_profile_display_name.intent: Write a user's CANONICAL display name through profiles.set_display_name — the named comm write stapel-profiles publishes, which owns the canon, the swappable model, get-or-create and the profile.changed emission. Returns None on success or the error key to answer with (profiles' own 400 key, error.503.profiles_not_configured when nothing is wired, error.503.profiles_unavailable when the call failed). Topology-independent; WorkspaceMember.display_name_hint is only a pre-profile placeholder, not this.

set_preferred_workspace.intent: Record (or clear) the person's explicit home workspace — the choice DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID yields to. Validated against active membership.

preferred_workspace_id_for.intent: The caller's stated home workspace id, or '' — active-membership filtered, so it goes quiet during a suspension.

can_create_workspace.intent: May this account found a workspace on this instance (WORKSPACE_CREATE_POLICY) — ask before drawing a '+ New space' control, so the button and the door agree.

instance_owner_ids.intent: User ids that own the instance — the OWNERs of DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID; empty when the deployment never declared one.

record_audit.intent: Append one line to a workspace's membership history (an event-store line, through the deployment's AUDIT_SINK) — call it from the service that OWNS a transition, never from a view, so a second door cannot come with a second chance to forget.

eventstore_sink.intent: The default journal sink: append to the core event store and flush, so a sibling worker's read right after the transition already sees the line. Swap via STAPEL_WORKSPACES["AUDIT_SINK"] (gateway-shaped callable) to ship the journal elsewhere.

history_page.intent: One anchor page of a workspace's membership history, newest first, workspace-scoped unconditionally — the read behind GET <id>/audit; use it instead of querying the stream by hand.

replay_legacy_rows.intent: Carry rows of the retired 0.24 audit table into the stream, ids and timestamps intact — the data path migration 0009 runs; not for new writes.
